Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-rays (1a and 1b) demonstrate a large, well-circumscribed, lobulated mass occupying the right hemithorax. This appearance is characteristic of a large soft tissue tumor such as a pleomorphic liposarcoma, which can grow to be quite large before causing symptoms like dyspnea due to mass effect. The other options (pulmonary embolism, pneumonia, pneumothorax, pulmonary fibrosis) do not present as a discrete, large, rounded mass on plain radiography. Pleural effusion typically presents with blunting of the costophrenic angle or a meniscus sign, rather than a distinct spherical mass with sharp borders as seen here.
